current.text: Yahoo lists him as questionable with an undisclosed issue. The newest note says he is healthy and has played in the preseason.
He is the projected starting center, with Acuff, LaVine, Murray and Ben Simmons. Simmons starts instead of DeAndre Hunter.
DeRozan, Westbrook and Schroder are gone from Sacramento. They took shots and assists away from him.
Experts expect his usage to rise and his assists and minutes to return to about 6 assists and 33 minutes.
Simmons starting next to him makes one expert a bit more cautious, because another ball handler shares the offense.
Raynaud and Cardwell are both out at least two weeks. Sabonis and Precious Achiuwa form the center rotation, with possible small ball using Simmons at center.
Experts do not expect Maxime Raynaud to cut his minutes or take his starting job.
Mike Miller runs the Kings offense this season. It is unclear whether he will run it through Sabonis.
Coach Ham calls him the Kings' best player.
Toronto has talked to the Kings about him before, and Sacramento might try to dump his contract.

Experts disagree on the trade risk. Most call a trade the main risk, since on a contender he could become a 23-minute backup. Lloyd thinks a trade is unlikely because of his contract, and another expert thinks he would keep most of his value after a trade.
His FG% and three-point percentage should bounce back from last season's lows.
Experts value him around round three in category leagues, as roughly a top 25 to 30 player with top 20 upside. One expert thinks taking him in round one is wrong.
Lloyd says his Yahoo rank of 34 is too low.
In an auction mock, 25 USD was called a reasonable price. He went for 24 USD.
Some drafters pass on him or push him back a few slots because of uncertainty about his role and the Kings' direction.

Experts disagree on the Kings' plans. Lloyd expects them to trade or sit veterans and finish near the bottom. Others expect them to try to win to stay out of the relegation zone, so Sabonis plays when available.
The Kings play 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21, so 11 games. They have 14 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: He is an elite, unselfish passer and rebounder. He is the best in the league at assists plus rebounds combined, and the numbers pile up when the offense runs through him.
He needs the ball to rack up assists, many of them from dribble handoffs, so his value depends on a big offensive role.
His rebounds and his FG% on high volume are league outliers. His turnovers are high and hurt the TO category.
He has never been a steals or blocks player and is a very poor shot blocker.
He is not a good three-point shooter and is a poor defender.
He is a much better points league player than category league player. His game is hard to build around in category leagues when taken early.
In 2025-26 he pulled his hamstring before the season, then had a rib injury, then a meniscus issue that ended in knee surgery.

note: He costs 25 USD on Yahoo and 37.3 USD on ESPN, and went for 41 USD in our league last season. Experts call 25 USD reasonable and see round-three value (rank about 25 to 34), so paying low 30s is fine but 40 USD is not. His elite rebounds, high-volume FG% and big-man assists fit punt TO builds best, but his 3 turnovers and weak FT%, threes and blocks make him hard to build around early. Early in the season, check whether his minutes climb back toward 33 and his assists toward 6 with Simmons starting next to him. Also watch for any trade news and clear up the Yahoo Q tag before the draft.
